summary:
Sverdlovsk Oblast has no legislation of its own on gender identity or sexual orientation and stands under the national framework of Russia, which applies in full; the oblast administration has added no protections of its own. What is documented at regional level is enforcement pressure and violence in Yekaterinburg, the oblast capital.

Reporting dated 21 October 2024 records that a gay man in Yekaterinburg was beaten and robbed after being lured into a fake date, and that a Yekaterinburg LGBTQ+ support group shut down after pressure. Together they show targeting in the oblast operating through private violence and through pressure on the organisations that would otherwise provide support.
tangentialFactors:
The Yekaterinburg robbery was not opportunistic street crime: the victim was drawn out through a purported date. Visitors who use dating platforms in the oblast are exposed to the same method.

Documented regional signal is confined to Yekaterinburg. No incidents or enforcement actions are recorded for other towns in the oblast, which reflects where reporting is concentrated rather than a demonstrated difference in risk.
localsOnly: For residents, the closure of a Yekaterinburg LGBTQ+ support group removes local counselling and community infrastructure. The same assessment records that survey respondents in the Ural area were more closeted toward relatives than the whole-study sample, indicating that disclosure within families carries a particular cost in the region.
outOfScopeNotes:
The legal outcome of the Yekaterinburg robbery and assault is not recorded, and no oblast-level figures for prosecutions, detentions or hate incidents are published.

Whether the Yekaterinburg support group closed under formal legal action or after informal pressure is not stated in the source.

No region-specific information on access to gender-affirming care or on document processing in the oblast is available; those matters are set by the national framework.
